author: p. k. quinn
title: Florida Panthers fall to Devils as losing streak extends - Central Broward News
text:
The Florida Panthers lost 5-1 to the New Jersey Devils on Tuesday at Prudential Center, extending their losing streak to three games. With a record of 30-28-3, the Panthers are now 10 points behind the second wild-card spot in the Eastern Conference with 21 games left in the season.
Forward Tomas Nosek returned from offseason surgery to make his season debut for Florida. “You cannot look at the math,” Nosek said. “When you start looking at the math, you’re gone. You need to just focus on next game and win the next game. That’s all there is.”
Panthers goaltender Sergei Bobrovsky made several key saves early in the first period, stopping attempts from Timo Meier and Paul Cotter. The Devils opened scoring at 12:10 when Arseny Gritsyuk scored on a 2-on-1 rush.
Anton Lundell tied the game for Florida shortly after a power play expired, notching his 200th NHL career point with a backhand goal past Jacob Markstrom at 14:37 of the first period.
“We’ve asked a lot of him,” head coach Paul Maurice said about Lundell’s increased role due to Aleksander Barkov’s injury. “One of the things he’s learning is the unusual level of fatigue that comes in the number one hole when you’re [on the] power play, penalty kill. Good for him scoring again. That may be the thing that comes out of him, that he believes he can put pucks to the net. We believe there’s offense there.”
The Devils regained control in the second period with Dougie Hamilton scoring off a rebound and Cody Glass tipping in another goal, making it 3-1 by 8:13.
In the third period, New Jersey limited Florida to two shots on goal and secured victory with empty-net goals from Dawson Mercer and Simon Nemec.
Bobrovsky recorded 28 saves for Florida while Markstrom stopped 20 of 21 shots for New Jersey. Bobrovsky also made eight high-danger saves during play.
“We had a tough one tonight,” Maurice said after the loss. “Sergei was good. Our goaltending was good. We got behind in the game. We were having a hard time generating, so we tried to do a whole bunch of different ways that weren’t particularly effective.”
Tomas Nosek commented on his return: “It’s been a long six months. I’m just so happy to be back in the locker room and around the guys.”
Maurice addressed areas for improvement: “There’s a certain way we move the puck, with an attitude coming into the offensive line, that I think we’ve gotten away from.”
Additional statistics show Lundell became only the fifth player from his draft class (2020) to reach 200 career points; Florida led New Jersey in high-danger shot attempts at even strength; Uvis Balinskis helped lead shots on goal when deployed; Bobrovsky stopped all ten third-period shots; A.J. Greer and Sandis Vilmanis combined for twelve hits.
The Panthers will end their road trip with back-to-back games starting Thursday against Columbus Blue Jackets at Nationwide Arena.
